challenger.dispersion_parameter: one global nu per target per fold
challenger.family: independent side Conway-Maxwell-Poisson with each side parameterized to preserve the frozen V2 expected side count
challenger.fold_fit_objective: mean joint side negative log probability on training fixtures strictly before validation start
challenger.mean_parameterization: solve CMP lambda so predictive mean matches frozen V2 side expected count
challenger.normalization: deterministic finite-support log-weight normalization with adaptive support checks
challenger.tie_rule: choose nu closest to 1.0; remaining tie choose lower nu

evaluation.advance_gate: pooled joint side LogS improves, joint side LogS wins at least 3/4 folds, pooled total RPS does not worsen, and fixed-line binary Log Loss does not worsen by more than 0.001
evaluation.uncertainty: weekly-block paired uncertainty is required before any later component promotion; Stage1 point estimates alone cannot promote

means.source: frozen V2 DynamicHierarchicalCountBaseline DEVELOPMENT walk-forward means

next_stage: Only if pooled CMP passes Stage1 may a separately preregistered hierarchical dispersion model be tested. Otherwise retain current target-specific distributions.
purpose: Test Conway-Maxwell-Poisson as a flexible side-count distribution around frozen V2 dynamic means, with Poisson nested at nu=1 and the current corners Poisson/NB2 mixture as the corners reference.

reference_distributions.corners: fixture-level 0.25 independent Poisson joint + 0.75 independent side-NB2 joint; common NB2 alpha refit on training history strictly before each DEVELOPMENT fold

research_context.external_direction: 2026 football research reports predictive benefit from CMP dispersion modeling and team-level dispersion heterogeneity; QFE tests the simpler pooled nested family first
research_context.qfe_evidence: goals NB2 was near-Poisson/inconclusive; corners NB2 improved binary markets but worsened total-count NLL, motivating a distribution family that permits both over- and under-dispersion
